_: Node configurations for each supported provider. Drop one into a PLUGIN node's 'configuration' with pluginId 'email'. Every one of them names a secret rather than holding a password: store the value with the engine's secret management first, under the name given in passwordSecret (or as <credentialId>.username / <credentialId>.password).

_notes: Requires an app password: Google account -> Security -> 2-Step Verification -> App passwords.
A normal account password is refused by Gmail's SMTP endpoint and comes back as SMTP_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, which this plugin never retries.
Google Workspace accounts may have SMTP AUTH disabled by an administrator.
smtp-relay.gmail.com on 465 with SSL_TLS is the alternative for Workspace relay; set smtpHost and security explicitly to use it.
gmail.subject: Order ${order.id} confirmed

_notes: SMTP AUTH is disabled tenant-wide by default on Microsoft 365. An administrator must enable it for the sending mailbox (Set-CASMailbox -SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled $false).
Security defaults or Conditional Access can block basic authentication regardless of that setting.
The from address must be the authenticated mailbox, or one it has Send As rights over. Microsoft enforces this at the server; no client setting works around it.
Port 25 with a connector is the high-volume alternative and needs no credentials — set authenticationRequired to false and security to NONE only if the connector is restricted by IP.
microsoft365.subject: Approval needed: ${request.title}

_notes: The username is the literal string 'apikey' for every account. It is not a secret and not derived from one.
The API key is the password, and needs only the Mail Send permission.
The from address must belong to a verified sender or an authenticated domain, or SendGrid refuses the message with a 550.
sendgrid.subject: Your receipt

_notes: The host is region-dependent: smtp.zoho.com, smtp.zoho.eu, smtp.zoho.in, smtp.zoho.com.au. The preset uses the .com endpoint; set smtpHost for any other region.
An application-specific password is required when two-factor authentication is on.
465 with SSL_TLS is also offered; the preset uses 587 with STARTTLS.
zoho.subject: Ticket ${ticket.id} updated

_notes: SES has no default host: the endpoint is regional, so smtpHost must be set. email-smtp.<region>.amazonaws.com.
The credentials are SES SMTP credentials, generated in the SES console. An AWS access key id and secret key will not authenticate here.
A new account is in the SES sandbox and can only send to verified addresses.
465 with SSL_TLS and 2587 / 2465 are also available where 587 is blocked by the network.
amazonSes.subject: Your order has shipped

_notes: The username is the domain's postmaster address; the password is that domain's SMTP password from the Mailgun dashboard.
EU domains use smtp.eu.mailgun.org — set smtpHost for those.
The from address must be on the sending domain.
mailgun.subject: Password reset requested
mailgun.body: Reset your password. The link expires in one hour.

_notes: An app password is required; the account password is refused.
Rate limits are low enough that this is a poor choice for anything but occasional mail.
yahoo.subject: Notification

_notes: Any SMTP server: a company relay, a hosted mailbox, a self-run Postfix.
587 with STARTTLS is the usual pairing. 465 expects SSL_TLS instead — a mismatch here produces SMTP_SSL_FAILED or SMTP_TLS_FAILED rather than a timeout.
The host may itself come from a variable, so one workflow can point at different relays per environment.
customSmtpAuthenticated.subject: [${environment}] ${notification.subject}

_notes: An internal relay that accepts mail from the engine's own network without credentials.
NONE means everything on the wire is readable by anything on the path. Legitimate inside a trusted network; wrong for anything reached over the internet.
No username or password is needed, and none should be configured: sending credentials over an unencrypted connection is worse than not authenticating.
internalRelayUnauthenticated.subject: Nightly reconciliation complete

_notes: Run this on its own from the designer to prove a configuration works. It performs DNS, TCP, TLS and AUTH and disconnects without sending anything.
Outputs email.connectionVerified, email.host, email.port and email.security.
